rules.title: Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources Delivery Requirement
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] Landlords must provide tenants with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit when commencing eviction or deciding not to offer a lease renewal. Anyone purchasing property out of foreclosure or from a lender must also deliver this notice to former owners or tenants asked to leave the property.
rules.coverage_conditions: The Ordinance applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston. [Question 5]
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility, or health facility are exempt. [Question 5]; Residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance, or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse are exempt. [Question 5]
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.
The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must also be delivered to any tenant
that is asked to leave a property. For example, if someone is purchasing a property
out of foreclosure, or from a bank or a mortgage lender, they must provide this
Notice to the former owners of the property, or any tenants that live in the
property.
